dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：**Reference Anything is an enhancement for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) `@` menu.** It brings files, sessions, local agents, web chats, cloud drives, and local plugins into one searchable menu, so you can mention the context you need without switching tools or copying content manually.

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：After typing `@`, you can browse and click items in the menu with your mouse, or use the keyboard to enter text, search, and narrow down the results. When a folder is selected, press `Tab` to enter it and continue browsing, or `Enter` to insert the folder reference.

Use one `@` menu to reference:

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：- 🧩 DSH commands and Skills
- 📁 Workspace files and folders
- 💬 DSH session history
- 🖥️ **Local Agent conversations:** bundled scanning and read-only parsers for 33 source formats, including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor; optional import into DSH through Chat Import. Live acceptance coverage is recorded separately.
- ✨ **Added by this plugin — highlight: Historical conversations from web chatbots including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and Kimi**
- ☁️ **Added by this plugin: Files from cloud drives connected through OpenList**
- 🧩 **Added by this plugin: Installed and configured local DSH plugins, without repeatedly hunting through directories**
dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：Beyond extending what `@` can reference, Reference Anything also enhances the `@` menu itself:

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：- Customize visible groups: enable or hide `Commands`, `Skills`, files, DSH sessions, local agent conversations, external conversations, cloud-drive files, and local plugins, then arrange them in any order
- Customize shortcuts: assign your own shortcuts to source groups, web providers, local agents, and cloud-drive mounts
- Customize result counts: set each group's collapsed row count and hard candidate cap independently
- Choose how to browse: expand or collapse individual groups, or use DSH's native scrolling list
- Enhanced visual icons and commands: distinguish reference sources with type icons and platform logos

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：
Native DSH display Reference Anything icon enhancements

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：Type `@`, search across enabled sources, and insert the selected reference into the current task. Each source keeps its own access and loading behavior: files use DSH's permission-constrained tools, DSH sessions use the native session-reference protocol, local agent transcripts are streamed straight off disk, cloud-drive files are fetched a window at a time over the drive's own API, and external conversation bodies are read on demand.

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：**The External conversations group** — and only that group — uses OpenCLI to reach AI chat sessions you are already logged into. By default it stores conversation titles locally and the agent fetches remote content on demand; an optional offline-mirror mode stores the latest complete bodies locally instead. **Local agent conversations need none of that**: those transcripts are already files on your own disk, so that group reads them directly, with no browser, no OpenCLI, and nothing mirrored.

dsh-reference-anything README · Introduction：> [!NOTE]
> DSH is currently in Beta, so its underlying capabilities and interfaces may change as it evolves. This plugin will adapt alongside those changes. Because of some current DSH limitations, parts of the implementation may not yet be ideal; we will continue to follow DSH updates and improve the plugin over time. See the relevant sections below for specific limitations and usage notes.

dsh-reference-anything README · 📦 Installation：This version is **v0.5.2**, with a declared minimum DSH SDK version of **`0.2.0-rc.2`**.

dsh-reference-anything README · Official desktop app：Reference Anything handles native references by default. If you explicitly enable the official `ui-reference` plugin in your profile, restart DSH and reload the page: the official plugin handles native references, and RA hides its duplicate file and DSH session candidates. Previously inserted RA file/session references still work; other RA sources are unaffected.

dsh-reference-anything README · Official desktop app：Official file and session sections follow RA's visibility switches and independent ordering, and retain its collapsed item counts and expand/collapse actions, including arrow-key, Enter, and Tab navigation. The official plugin still handles reference insertion, copying, and previews. Select “No collapse (native)” to show the full list; unsupported candidate formats also fall back to the full list.

dsh-reference-anything README · Official desktop app：After Tab enters a file directory, RA pauses searches in other sources and the menu shows only files. Returning to the root restores other sources. Expand/collapse actions use gray text.

Download the official desktop app from the [DeepSeek Harness website](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/), open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `dsh-reference-anything`, and follow the prompts to install and enable it. Restart DSH if asked, then open **Settings → Reference Anything**.

dsh-reference-anything README · Official desktop app：Desktop uses a separate plugin profile; plugins installed in the Web profile are not automatically enabled in Desktop. See the [official desktop documentation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/desktop/README.md).

dsh-reference-anything README · DSH Market：Open [Reference Anything on DSH Market](https://dshmarket.com/p/Chael-Chael/dsh-reference-anything/), or search for `dsh-reference-anything` in the in-app market. If the market is not installed, use **Add plugin** with `dshmarket` in Desktop; for Web, run:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket
```

dsh-reference-anything README · Web CLI：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-reference-anything
```

The installed version depends on the selected channel; this README describes v0.5.2.

dsh-reference-anything README · Optional: Connect web AI chats：Only web chats need this step. Local sources work without it. Sign into the desired platforms in your browser. OpenCLI is installed with this plugin; adapter setup still needs npm.

dsh-reference-anything README · Optional: Connect web AI chats：After installing the DSH plugin, open `Settings → Reference Anything → Availability check` in DSH (restart DSH first if this settings entry is not yet visible), then click **One-click setup**. It uses OpenCLI 2.0.0 installed as a runtime dependency and updated together with this plugin; installs the bundled adapters for all six platforms; starts or refreshes Browser Bridge; and opens the OpenCLI Browser Bridge page in the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/opencli/ildkmabpimmkaediidaifkhjpohdnifk). Confirm the extension installation, then return and click **Recheck setup**. Any remaining failed check displays its own recovery action.

dsh-reference-anything README · Optional: Connect web AI chats：For a custom global OpenCLI, install it manually and enter its full executable path in settings. The default opencli always uses the plugin dependency:

```powershell
npm install --global "@jackwener/opencli@2.0.0"
opencli plugin install file:///C:/path/to/dsh-reference-anything/opencli-plugin
opencli daemon restart
```

dsh-reference-anything README · Optional: Connect web AI chats：Replace `C:/path/to/dsh-reference-anything` with the repository location. Browser extensions cannot be silently installed from a webpage; confirm the installation in the Chrome Web Store, or download an extension package from [OpenCLI Releases](https://github.com/jackwener/opencli/releases) and use “Load unpacked.” If the browser blocks the store popup, the settings page keeps a normal fallback link. When multiple browser profiles are connected, select and apply one directly in the failed check. OpenCLI updates with this plugin; the browser store updates the extension separately.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🚀 Usage：Reference Anything registers eight sources in the native DSH `@` menu rather than introducing a separate search interface. Settings let you choose which groups appear, their order, their collapsed row count, their hard candidate cap, and whether groups use plugin-owned collapse actions or the native scrolling list. A separate one-click control switches the visible picker back to DSH's official file/session list without stopping the plugin, synchronization service, local data, or model-facing tools; the same control restores the Reference Anything picker at any time.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🚀 Usage：1. Type `@` to browse sources, or enter a keyword such as `@cache-design`.
2. Click a result, or select it with the arrow keys and press `Enter`. For workspace folders, `Tab` opens the folder and `Enter` inserts a reference.
3. Add your request and send it: “Use this Codex conversation and project folder to check whether the earlier plan has been implemented.”

dsh-reference-anything README · 🚀 Usage：For web chats, complete the connection steps above, then choose platforms, browser profile, storage mode, and history range under **Settings → Reference Anything → Web AI conversation sync settings** and start syncing. For cloud files, connect OpenList and add a mount in Settings.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🚀 Usage：The default **Read bodies on demand** mode stores only the title index locally and uses the browser when an agent needs the conversation. Choose **Store full bodies locally** for offline reading and full-text search. The plugin checks for new versions when it loads; release notes are available in Settings, and installed updates take effect after restarting DSH.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🚀 Usage：Release-card demo images load from GitHub only when their card is displayed. They require network access; text and navigation remain available if an image fails to load.

> [!NOTE]
> OpenCLI may open or reuse browser windows while syncing web chats or reading bodies. Keep them available until the operation finishes. Sync speed depends on the platform, history size, and browser connection.

dsh-reference-anything README · Shortcut examples：These examples use the current defaults. After changing shortcuts, use the values shown in Settings.

| Input | What it finds |
| --- | --- |
| `@file:README` | Workspace files and folders |
| `@session:` | DSH session history |
| `@agent:` / `@codex:` | Local agent history / Codex only |
| `@chat:` / `@chatgpt:cache` | Web chats / matching ChatGPT chats |
| `@drive:` | Connected cloud drives |
| `@plugin:` | Local DSH plugins |
| `@command:` / `@skill:` | Commands / Skills |

dsh-reference-anything README · Shortcut examples：Under **General**, set shortcuts for groups, web providers, local agents, and cloud mounts. Separate multiple shortcuts with commas: set the file group to `file,f`, then use `@f:README`. A shortcut can target multiple sources. Full-width colons (`：`) are also supported.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🧩 One `@` menu, multiple sources：The `@` menu contains eight groups: `Commands`, `Skills`, `Files and folders`, `DSH sessions`, `Local agent conversations`, `External conversations`, `Cloud drive files`, and `All local plugins`. The cloud-drive group browses folders and supported files from drives connected through OpenList; access is read-only, and connections are managed in Settings. Each group shows six rows before its expand action by default and accepts a separate hard candidate cap from 1 to 50. In collapse mode, each expand action reveals five more rows and updates the mounted menu without jumping back to the top; collapse restores the configured compact count. The external-conversation group keeps its sync action first and updates that row and the visible results in place while synchronization runs and completes. Under `Settings → Reference Anything → General`, you can enable or disable groups, reorder them, assign an optional custom shortcut (for example `f` for Files, then use `@f:notes`), and choose **Collapse / expand** or **Native DSH scrolling**.
dsh-reference-anything README · ⌨️ @Commands — DSH native commands：To browse commands, use `@command:`; selecting one hands `/command` back to DSH's native slash pipeline.
dsh-reference-anything README · 🛠️ @Skills — DSH skill library：To browse skills, use `@skill:`; selecting one inserts `/skill` for DSH's native skill handling.

dsh-reference-anything README · 📁 @Files and folders — workspace files and directories：Type `@file:` in the input box to browse files and folders through DSH's official file-reference Remote.

**Features:** - Uses the official `@path` / `@"path with spaces"` grammar and canonical file candidate service - Files and folders become native references; press `Tab` on a folder to browse inside it, or `Enter` to insert it
section: 📁 @Files and folders — workspace files and directories

text:
dsh-reference-anything README · 💬 @DSH sessions — DSH session history：Type `@session:` to browse DSH sessions through the official session-reference Remote.

Selected sessions use DSH's canonical `dsh-session:` mention and native session appearance. Snapshot preparation and resolution remain owned by DSH rather than this plugin.

dsh-reference-anything README · 💬 @DSH sessions — DSH session history：The bundled 0.26.3 reader also supports **oh-my-pi (`@omp:`)** from `~/.omp/agent/sessions`; importing requires Chat Import 0.26.3 or newer.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：Type `@agent:` to search and reference conversations saved by other local agent tools.

New sources: **Copilot VS Code (`@copilot-vscode:`)**, **Copilot CLI (`@copilot-cli:`)** and **Doubao Desktop (`@doubao:`)**. Doubao can only reference conversations whose bodies are cached locally; open the conversation in Doubao first if it is missing.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：All 33 sources use bundled read-only scanners and parsers derived from dsh-chat-import. Scanning and references work without installing Chat Import. Source switches, additional directories and workspace scope still apply; settings show source paths, counts and scan errors. Enter inserts a reference, including recoverable images through DSH attachments; viewing images requires a vision-capable model. Confirmed empty conversations are hidden; read errors remain visible. Local references now store a readable source, path and session ID; reselect references created with the old local URI protocol.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：When you send local references, the plugin appends one aggregated background after each user message. The model reads `ref: {source, path, sessionId}` with a content `revision`. `reference_list` discovers local sessions; `reference_read` reads `messages`, `tools` or `images`; `reference_search` searches message/tool text; `reference_image` returns actual pixels.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：Use `from` for both scope and starting position: `messages` uses `messageId`; `tools` uses `toolId` with an optional owning `messageId`; `images` uses `imageId` with an optional owning `messageId`. Copy the complete `next` object into `from` to continue. Long text uses a Unicode code-point `textOffset`, preserving every remaining character rather than keeping only the head and tail. Source-provided summaries use `role: "summary"`; source limitations use an English `notice`. Source content is never translated.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：`reference-mention.maxTextBytes` caps all new reference contexts in one pre-step batch at 16 KiB by default; estimated remaining context can reduce it. `reference-tool.maxTextBytes` separately caps each local tool text result at 16 KiB. Unknown capacity leaves only bounded metadata and a notice; metadata that cannot fit fails explicitly. Previews contain a continuous recent suffix, with a continuation for an oversized final message. Images have a separate 10 MiB limit.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：Every new read checks the enabled source, allowed real path and session identity; no per-session grant is needed for local references. After a version change, restart `reference_read` with the same `ref`, `part: "messages"`, and omit both `revision` and `from`. No full-text snapshots or cross-call parsed-body caches are saved. Other sources retain their existing URI-based protocol under `external_reference_list` and `external_reference_read`.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：Import status, session import and handoff summaries use the optional Chat Import API. Install or upgrade the independent plugin from settings when needed; Reference Anything does not install it on startup. An unavailable API leaves import status unknown and does not stop local scanning or reference reading. Tab retains the configured import and summary actions and confirmation flow.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：The scanner runs in a separate process and caches metadata for 30 seconds. Parsing a reference may still read its complete source before returning a page. Source code and icons retain their MIT licenses (see `vendor/chat-import-reader/` and `images/agents/LICENSE`). Maintainers update both snapshots with `npm run vendor:sync -- <built-dsh-chat-import-directory>`; see the vendor README for checks before shipping.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：- Automatically detects conversation history and shows the number found for each agent
- Lets you enable agents independently or choose a custom history folder
- Searches all detected conversations by default, with an option to limit results to the current workspace

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs：References read local history without modifying it. Import and handoff-summary actions are separate operations through Chat Import. Claude Code and Codex adapters have been checked against real transcripts; other formats are primarily fixture-tested and may vary by tool version. Database reads for opencode, mimocode, and zcode require `node:sqlite` in the DSH host runtime.
section: 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs

text: dsh-reference-anything README · 🧩 @Local plugins — installed and configured plugins：Use `@plugin:` to find plugins. Settings can also show only running plugins or hide official DeepSeek plugins. Under **Settings → Reference Anything → General**, the **All local plugins** switch enables or disables this group immediately; the choice is saved. It is enabled by default, with six collapsed rows and a candidate cap of 50.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🧩 @Local plugins — installed and configured plugins：The list uses the active DSH loader's composed entries and lifecycle state, supplemented by declared profile bundles and installed packages with DSH bundle/client metadata. Ordinary dependencies are excluded. Running, disabled, and not-running states describe host entries; packages without a host entry are shown as not running. Selecting a plugin inserts its name and, when available, a native reference to its real local directory. File access still uses DSH's existing tools and permissions.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🌐 @External conversations — external conversation platforms：Supports historical conversations from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and Kimi.

**Store full bodies locally** enables offline reading of synchronized text; it does not mean attachments are saved offline. Automatic and startup sync are off by default and can be enabled in Settings. **Platform filtering:**

dsh-reference-anything README · 🌐 @External conversations — external conversation platforms：- Use `@chatgpt:cache` or `@claude:refactor` to filter a specific platform
- Short aliases are also accepted, such as `@gpt:` and `@ds:`
- Entering `@claude` alone lists recent conversations for that platform

**Search capabilities:**

- **Title match:** fuzzy search on conversation titles

- **Content search:** available only in **Store full bodies locally** mode; if title matches are insufficient, synchronized bodies are searched and matching excerpts are shown in the candidate list

dsh-reference-anything README · 🌐 @External conversations — external conversation platforms：- **Provider and account isolation:** history is maintained separately by Provider and account scope

- `@` search uses the account scope cached by the latest sync and never probes the browser; after a sync observes an account switch, it exposes only that account while older rows remain available in conversation management for cleanup

dsh-reference-anything README · 🌐 @External conversations — external conversation platforms：**Reference display:** after selection, the draft shows a native removable DSH reference with the Provider logo. Its stable serialized form is:

```

Opening the source URL happens only in the UI; the URL is never injected into model context. A Web conversation reference initially contains only a safe pointer; if the model needs the body, it calls `external_reference_read` on demand.

dsh-reference-anything README · 🤖 Model-facing Protocol：- The agent calls `external_reference_read({ uri, limit, cursor })` only when it needs the body. Turns in each page are in chronological order, and pagination moves from newer pages toward older ones.
- For the initial `deferred=true` item, the first call passes only `uri` and does not send an empty `nextCursor`.
- In offline-mirror mode, `external_reference_read` paginates over the current revision. In metadata-only mode, each read requests content from the Provider again and validates the cached account scope inside that same browser operation. Missing, account-mismatch, and fetch errors instruct the agent to ask for a Provider sync before retrying.
- `before` is kept only as a deprecated compatibility parameter and cannot be combined with `cursor`.
- A mention or `external_reference_list` grants the current task permission to read that URI; unauthorized URIs are rejected.
- Each conversation keeps only the latest revision. Cursors for older revisions expire after content changes.
- `reference_attachment_read` validates the task grant and, for Web conversations, verifies that the active provider account still matches the acc

dsh-reference-anything README · 💾 Sync and Storage：The `reference_anything` storage domain contains:

- `conversations`: Provider, account scope, remote ID, current revision, and integrity state
- `revisions`: content hash, turn count, active branch, and chunk manifest
- `turn_chunks`: immutable chunks of 50 turns
- `attachments`: stable locators and metadata without temporary signed URLs
- `sync_states`: Provider cursor, profile, progress, and errors

dsh-reference-anything README · 💾 Sync and Storage：Remote records are marked `remoteMissing` only after a full remote pagination pass succeeds. The sync history range defaults to unlimited; once a day count is set, web chats last updated before that range are deleted locally and skipped by later syncs. DOM fallback is used only after an API request fails, and fallback data is always marked `partial=true`.

dsh-reference-anything README · 💾 Sync and Storage：In `metadata-only` mode, the current browser account is checked inside the same detail operation that reads a referenced body; reads are rejected when it does not match the account scope cached by sync. Conversation management includes bulk actions for records marked `remoteMissing` and for local chats owned by non-current accounts of providers whose current account is known.
